_comment: Practice Arena — konfigurace herni vrstvy Academy (Faze A).
DATA ONLY. Zadny HTML, zadna biologie. Vsechny polozky se GENERUJI z
pathway/model.json a academy_data/lessons.json — tenhle soubor drzi jen
pravidla hry: prahy hodnosti, XP vzorec, decay mastery, kriteria odznaku
a kratke UI texty. build_practice.py to zapece do stranky, verify_practice.py
kontroluje, ze kazde kriterium odznaku ma metriku, kterou engine skutecne
pocita (odznak bez merene metriky by se nedal nikdy ziskat).
Prahy nize jsou NAVRH, ne mereni — po pilotu se prenastavuji tady, ne v kodu.

ranks.name: Curious
ranks.blurb: Recall: what the parts are and which way the arrows point.

ranks.name: Student
ranks.blurb: Mechanism: why the pathway is built the way it is.

ranks.name: Rotation Student
ranks.blurb: Prediction: what happens when you change something.

ranks.name: Graduate
ranks.blurb: Reading data: what a result does and does not support.

ranks.name: Postdoc
ranks.blurb: Judgement: how strong is this evidence, really.

ranks.name: Principal Investigator
ranks.blurb: Design: what would you measure first, and why that.

rankup.note: Rank-up is a short mixed board, not an automatic threshold. Ranks 4-6 additionally require a calibration score, because from Graduate on the questions are about judgement, not recall.

confidence.hint: Say how sure you are before you see the answer. Being right while unsure is worth less than being right while sure — and being sure while wrong is worth nothing.

mastery.note: Mastery is what you can do now; XP is what you have done. Only mastery decays.

badges.name: Predictor
badges.criterion: 8 / 25 / 60 correct predictions made before the reveal, across at least 4 lessons
badges.why: Prediction is the first step that cannot be faked by recognition.

badges.name: Pathway Architect
badges.criterion: Wire a full route correctly at the hard level — direct and indirect steps distinguished, no hints
badges.why: Knowing the parts is not knowing the wiring.

badges.name: Calibrated
badges.criterion: Brier score 0.18 / 0.13 / 0.10 or better over your last 50 judgements
badges.why: The one measurable habit that separates a scientist from a well-read reader.

badges.name: Core Architecture
badges.criterion: Mastery 3 or better on every node the Core lessons cover
badges.why: Coverage, not streaks: the map has no dark patch left in the core.

badges.name: Confounder Spotter
badges.criterion: Name what a result does NOT show, 5 / 15 times
badges.why: Most over-claiming is one unnoticed second explanation.

badges.name: Methods Reader
badges.criterion: 8 / 20 findings in Paper Autopsy across at least 5 kinds of weakness
badges.why: The methods section is where a paper is actually decided.

badges.name: n = 3 Skeptic
badges.criterion: Name the sample size as the limit 10 times -- and do not blame the sample when the paper's own limitation is something else
badges.why: Scepticism that fires at everything is not scepticism.

badges.name: Honest Unknown
badges.criterion: 10 correct \u201copen question\u201d calls in Frontier, without marking settled mechanisms as open
badges.why: Knowing where the field stops is knowledge, not a gap in it.

badges.name: Source Hunter
badges.criterion: 20 correct study IDs, at least 3 of them weakening the claim
badges.why: A claim you cannot trace is a claim you are repeating.

badges.name: Falsifier
badges.criterion: In a Research Challenge, run an experiment that can come out either way before one that can only confirm -- in 3 challenges
badges.why: The experiment worth paying for is the one that can come out either way.

games.name: Daily 5
games.blurb: Two you have seen, two new, one a level up. Three minutes.

games.name: Signal Sprint
games.blurb: Sixty seconds of arrows: does this one activate or inhibit?

games.name: Wire the Pathway
games.blurb: Rebuild a route from loose parts — and get the direct steps right.

games.name: Perturbation Lab
games.blurb: Set the controls, predict the readout before it is revealed.

games.name: What It Doesn't Show
games.blurb: One experiment from a lesson, four conclusions. Which one does it not prove?

games.name: Paper Autopsy
games.blurb: One real paper. Which limit of its design (sample, species, dose, length) matters here?

games.name: Find the Evidence
games.blurb: A claim from the map. Which study in the Atlas is it standing on?

games.name: Frontier
games.blurb: Established, emerging, contested or open? Say where the field actually is.

copy.hubLede: Eight games built on the Atlas's own pathway model and its own studies. Points reward calibration, not speed — and nothing here rewards simply showing up.
copy.progressLede: Your progress is the pathway itself. Grey nodes are the ones you have not been tested on yet; hatched ones are questions the field has not closed, so they never fill in.
copy.noJs: This page needs JavaScript for scoring and for saving progress in this browser. The practice questions themselves are below in full, with answers — the page is readable and usable without it.
copy.storageNote: Progress lives in this browser only. No account, nothing sent anywhere. Export it if you want to move it.
copy.openNote: Open questions never reach full mastery. That is not a bug in the game — the field has not closed them.
copy.phaseB: Ranks 4 to 6 are about judgement rather than recall: what a result does not show, which study a claim stands on, and how settled the field actually is.
copy.lockedNote: more games open as you rank up
copy.shareArena: I've reached {xp} XP ({rank}) in the mTOR Practice Arena on Oliver's mTOR Atlas. Can you beat me?
copy.shareQual: I scored {score}/{n} on the mTOR Qualifying Exam on Oliver's mTOR Atlas and placed as {rank}. Can you beat me?

qual._comment: Qualifying Exam /academy/qual/ — zkratka pro odborniky. Zarazeni na hodnost podle skore a kalibrace; PI se nezkousi, ziska se jen v Arene. Zadne XP za polozky, zadny odznak.

handItems.prompt: Rapamycin raises AKT Ser473 phosphorylation in a cancer cell line. Which experiment best separates released S6K1–IRS-1 feedback from a direct off-target action of the drug on AKT?
options: Repeat at ten times the dose and check that the rise gets larger
Remove the upstream route (knock down IRS-1, or block IGF-1R/PI3K) and repeat: if released feedback is the cause, the rise should largely disappear
Blot for phospho-S6 to confirm that mTORC1 was inhibited
Repeat the experiment in a second cell line
handItems.explain: The feedback hypothesis names a route: S6K1 normally restrains IRS-1, so the AKT rise should need IRS-1 and the receptor above it. Cutting that route tests the hypothesis directly; a drug acting on AKT itself would survive it. Phospho-S6 only shows the drug reached mTORC1, and a higher dose or another cell line changes the size of the effect without telling the two explanations apart. ORE2006 blocked the IGF-1 receptor for exactly this reason.

handItems.prompt: You want to show that an effect of rapamycin goes through mTOR rather than through some other target of the drug. Which control is the strongest?
options: A second batch of rapamycin from another supplier
Express an mTOR whose FRB domain cannot bind FKBP12–rapamycin: if those cells no longer show the effect, it goes through mTOR
Show that the effect reverses after the drug is washed out
handItems.explain: Rapamycin acts by bringing FKBP12 onto the FRB domain of mTOR (CHO1996 solved that interface). A point mutant there keeps the kinase working but makes it blind to the drug, so an effect that disappears in those cells must run through mTOR. Dose–response, a second batch and washout all describe the drug, not its target.

handItems.prompt: An hour of rapamycin leaves AKT Ser473 phosphorylation untouched; a day of rapamycin lowers it in some cell types but not in others. What best explains this?
options: Prolonged rapamycin can block assembly of new mTORC2, and how much depends on the cell type
S6K1 phosphorylates Ser473 directly, so its loss shows up only late
The antibody loses sensitivity in cells treated for long
handItems.explain: mTORC2 is not acutely sensitive to rapamycin, but over many hours the drug–FKBP12 complex can bind free mTOR and keep it from joining new mTORC2 (SAR2006). Cell types differ in how strongly this happens, which is why a timecourse, not one time point, decides what a rapamycin experiment shows about mTORC2.

handItems.prompt: Genetically heterogeneous mice given rapamycin from late middle age live longer on average. Which conclusion does that result NOT carry?
options: Inhibiting mTORC1 with a drug can extend lifespan in a mammal
Treatment started late in life can still have an effect
The same benefit will appear in people at doses they tolerate well
The effect is not confined to one inbred strain
handItems.explain: HAR2009 used three test sites and genetically mixed mice, which is why it supports a mammalian, late-onset and not strain-specific effect. Nothing in it measures human lifespan, human dosing or human tolerability; that step needs human data the study does not have.
